photo.caption: Parshvanatha, the 23rd Tirthankara, revived Jainism and ahimsa in the 9th century BCE, which led to a radical animal-rights movement in South Asia.
photo.description: India, madhya pradesh, jina parshvanatha dalla tempèesta, 600-700

photo.caption: The c. 5th-century CE Tamil philosopher Valluvar, in his Tirukkural, taught ahimsa and moral vegetarianism as personal virtues. The plaque in this statue of Valluvar at an animal sanctuary in South India describes the Kural's teachings on ahimsa and non-killing, summing them up with the definition of veganism.
photo.description: Valluvar Statue at Almighty Animal Sanctuary in Tiruvallur, Tamil Nadu, India. The plaque in Tamil describes the couplets 260 and 324 from the "Shunning Meat-eating" and "Non-killing" chapters of the Tirukkural, respectively, and gives the definition of Veganism ("Nanisaivam"). source : https://www.library.senthamil.org/142.htm (There are many English translations available. please find and verify) poem : 260 கொல்லான் புலாலை மறுத்தானைக் கைகூப்பி எல்லா உயிரும் தொழும். All lives shall lift their palms to him Who eats not flesh nor kills with whim
